question: What is a primary goal of providing wound care in a home setting?

options.A: Ensuring complete sterile surgical theater conditions
options.B: Promoting moist wound healing and preventing infection
options.C: Eliminating the need for any family caregiver involvement
options.D: Reducing the cost of hospital building maintenance

explanation: Home wound care focuses heavily on creating an optimal healing environment while keeping the wound free of pathogens. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h1)

question: Why is managing wounds at home more challenging than in a hospital ward?

options.A: Nurses are not allowed to touch dressings outside hospitals
options.B: Patients refuse all forms of medication at home
options.C: Wounds heal significantly slower outside clinical buildings
options.D: Home environments have varying conditions and limited equipment

explanation: Limited resources and unpredictable home settings require nurses to adapt their clinical techniques safely. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h1)

question: What color tissue in a wound bed typically indicates healthy granulation tissue?
explanation: Granulation tissue is highly vascularized and appears red or pink, signifying active tissue repair. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h2)

question: A nurse measuring a wound for tunneling should use which tool and method?

options.A: Visual estimation without touching the wound bed
options.B: A standard household tape measure on the skin surface
options.C: An ultrasound scanner placed over the dressing
options.D: A sterile probe to gently map hidden passageways

explanation: Tunneling and undermining require careful exploration with a sterile instrument to determine true depth and direction. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h2)

question: What is the single most effective way to prevent the spread of infection during home care?

options.A: Closing all windows in the bedroom
options.C: Spraying the room with strong disinfectants

explanation: Hand hygiene interrupts the transmission of microorganisms between the patient, nurse, and environment. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h3)

question: When is an alcohol-based hand rub NOT appropriate for hand hygiene?

options.A: When entering the patient's home for the visit
options.B: After removing a pair of clean non-sterile gloves
options.C: When hands are visibly soiled with dirt or body fluids
options.D: Before opening a fresh package of sterile gauze

explanation: Visible organic matter interferes with the efficacy of alcohol rubs, requiring physical removal with soap and water. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h3)

question: Which dressing type is best suited for a wound with heavy exudate requiring high absorption?
explanation: Foam dressings possess high absorptive capacity, making them ideal for managing heavy drainage. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h4)

question: Why is a hydrogel dressing prescribed for a dry necrotic wound?

options.A: It absorbs massive amounts of fluid quickly
options.B: It completely seals the wound against all air exchange
options.C: It provides rigid structural support to broken bones
options.D: It donates moisture to soften and rehydrate dead tissue

explanation: Hydrogels add moisture to dry environments, facilitating autolytic debridement of hard, necrotic tissue. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h4)

question: What should a nurse do if an old dressing sticks tightly to the wound bed?

options.A: Pull it off rapidly to finish the task quickly
options.B: Leave the old dressing in place indefinitely
options.C: Scrape it away using a dry metal spatula
options.D: Moisten it with sterile normal saline before removal

explanation: Moistening adhered dressings prevents trauma to newly formed granulation tissue during removal. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h5)

question: In which direction should a nurse cleanse a wound during a dressing change?

options.A: From the center of the wound outward
options.B: In a random zig-zag motion across the skin
options.C: From the outer edges inward toward the center
options.D: Strictly from the bottom of the wound to the top

explanation: Cleaning from the cleanest area (the wound center) outward prevents tracking contaminants into the wound bed. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h5)

question: Which sign is a localized indicator of wound infection?

options.C: Complete absence of any fluid drainage

explanation: Spreading erythema and rising pain levels are classic inflammatory signs of a developing wound infection. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h6)

question: What immediate action should be taken if a surgical wound experiences evisceration at home?

options.A: Gently push the exposed abdominal organs back inside
options.B: Wait until the scheduled clinic appointment next week
options.C: Apply tight adhesive tape directly across the open organs
options.D: Cover the exposed tissues with sterile saline-soaked dressings

explanation: Moist sterile coverings protect exposed organs from drying out while emergency transport is arranged. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h6)

question: Why is the return-demonstration method valuable when teaching home caregivers?

options.A: It replaces the requirement for sterile equipment
options.B: It allows the nurse to sleep while the family works
options.C: It eliminates the need for any written instructional pamphlets
options.D: It proves the caregiver can perform the technique correctly

explanation: Watching the caregiver perform the task ensures safe and accurate replication of the dressing change at home. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h7)

question: Besides dressing techniques, what other key topic should be included in home wound education?

options.A: Methods to disinfect hospital operating rooms
options.B: How to perform minor plastic surgery
options.C: The manufacturing process of medical gauze

explanation: Tissue healing requires systemic support through proper nutrition, fluid intake, and pressure redistribution. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h7)

question: What essential detail must always be included in wound documentation?

options.A: Exact wound dimensions and tissue types
options.B: The brand of soap used by the patient's family
options.C: The political opinions of the household members
options.D: The cost of the dressing supplies purchased

explanation: Objective measurements and tissue descriptions are necessary to track healing progress accurately. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h8)

question: Why is prompt communication between the home nurse and physician crucial for wound care?

options.A: It prevents nurses from having to write clinical notes
options.B: It fulfills a legal requirement to call doctors every hour
options.C: It allows for timely treatment adjustments if complications arise
options.D: It guarantees that the patient will never need rehospitalization

explanation: Reporting worsening signs quickly enables the physician to modify therapy, such as ordering antibiotics or new dressings. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h8)
